props.title: We treat engineering standards as the product.
props.lede: Most software fails slowly: it ships, it works, and eighteen months later nobody can change it safely. We build so that the second year is cheaper than the first.

props.heading: Five stages. Nothing skipped when the schedule tightens.

cards.title: Discover
cards.body: We map the real constraint before proposing anything. It is usually not the one in the brief.

cards.title: Architect
cards.body: Schema, boundaries, and failure modes on paper, approved by you before code exists.

cards.title: Build
cards.body: Two-week increments. Every pull request reviewed by a second engineer, CI green before merge.

cards.title: Harden
cards.body: Load tests, accessibility audit, performance budget enforced, dependency and secrets review.

cards.title: Ship & support
cards.body: Monitoring, an on-call rotation, and a documented handover your own team can act on.

props.heading: Most agencies say “quality”. Here is ours, as numbers.

content.text: These are contractual, not aspirational. If a build misses one it does not ship, and you do not pay for the sprint that fixes it.
